1.

Heard Sri Amit Daga, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Srijan Mehrotra, learned counsel for the informant as well as Sri Neeraj Kumar Sharma, learned AGA for the State-respondent and perused the record.

2. The instant bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. has been filed with a prayer to enlarge the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 219 of 2022, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B IPC,
Police Station Nai Mandi, District Muzaffar Nagar, during the pendency of trial.

entities.text: Police Station Nai Mandi, District Muzaffar Nagar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
3. The first information report in brief states that the husband, father-in-law and mother-in-law of the informant made forged signatures and in collusion with the bank employees transferred Rs.
9,50,000/- from her bank account in the account of her mother-in-law.

sentences.text: 4. Counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant was not named in the first information report.
There is no allegation against the applicant in the entire first information report.
In fact, the informant had issued a cheque of Rupees four lakhs fifty thousand dated 07.03.2022 to the applicant.
The said cheque was dishonored on 20.05.2022 on account of insufficient fund.

Subsequently, on 25.03.2023 the informant gave a second statement to the Investigating Officer,
wherein another version was narrated by her, she stated that the aforesaid cheque was given by the named co-accused Sharad Gupta (husband of the informant) to the applicant.

It is contended that after the dishonor of the said cheque, the applicant instituted the proceedings under Section 138 of N.I. Act numbered as Complaint Case No. 9589 of 2022 (Rahul Jain Vs. Smt. Priti).

entities.text: Complaint Case No. 9589 of 2022 (Rahul Jain Vs. Smt. Priti)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In order to harass the applicant, the informant in his second statement has falsely implicated him.
In the proceedings under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, the informant has been summoned.
The second statement, is an after thought and it discredit the prosecution case.
Even otherwise the genuineness of the signature of the informant on the said cheque is still to be ascertained in appropriate proceedings.

The co-accused Ashish Singh, who was also named by the informant in her second statement, has been granted bail by this Court in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 21695 of 2023 vide order dated 15.05.2023.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 21695 of 2023
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The applicant also claims parity.

The applicant is in jail since 19.06.2023 having no criminal history and in case he is enlarged on bail, he will not misuse the said liberty.
5.
Learned AGA and learned counsel for the informant have opposed the prayer for bail but could not satisfactorily dispute the aforesaid submissions from the record.
6. After hearing the rival contentions of learned counsel for the parties, this Court prima facie finds that the applicant was not not named in the first information report.
The name of the applicant was introduced in the second statement of the informant recorded on 25.03.2023.

The identically placed co-accused Ashish Singh has been granted bail by this Court and further the applicant has remained confined for almost two months and after submission of the charge-sheet there is no hope of early conclusion of trial, more so when no reasonable apprehension has been brought to the fore by the State that the applicant, if enlarged on bail, would either tamper with the evidence or delay the trial or intimidate the witness, without commenting on the merits of the case, I am of the opinion that the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
7.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move bail cancellation application before this Court.
